title: Does it work on crypto? His 9 EMA / 20 SMA / 200 SMA rules on 16 Binance perps, plus every claim measured
market: Crypto: 16 Binance USDT perps (ARB AVAX BNB BTC CRV DOGE ETH FIL INIT LINK SOL STRK SUI TIA XRP ZEC), spot cross check BTC/ETH/SOL
data: /Volumes/Moon 26/tick_data/binance/futures_klines_1m/<SYM>USDT/<SYM>USDT_1m_<start>_<end>.parquet, 2020-01-01 -> 2026-10-25 (each coin from its listing date); spot: spot_klines_1m/. Resampled to 5m/15m/1h/4h/1d (1m/2m built on the fly for the US-session test).

headline.label: Best in-sample crypto version (swing_reclaim20, 1d) out of sample, 16 coins, after costs
headline.value: -0.13R per trade OOS (281 trades) vs +1.10R in-sample; random entries with the same exits +0.18R

stats.costs: 0.05% Binance taker + 0.02% slippage per side (0.14% round trip), charged in R. Zero-cost version shown too. 1% risk per trade, all coins in exit-time order.

claims.claim: Never trade a flat / sideways 20 SMA, it is chop
claims.test: 1h, 16 coins, both sides: pullback trigger trades (over bar high, stop bar low, 2R) bucketed by 20 SMA slope (ATR/bar, 5-bar lookback). Plus forward 20-bar trend efficiency by |slope| quintile.
claims.result: flat-slope trades avg 0.071R (35.7% win, n=15406) vs sloped buckets [0.007, -0.0, 0.015]R. 15m flat: 0.007R. Trend efficiency flattest->steepest quintile: 0.2308 -> 0.2195

claims.claim: Best slope is about 45 degrees; too steep = overextended, too flat = no momentum
claims.test: Same trades, slope buckets. '45 degrees' depends on chart zoom, so slope is ATR per bar (video leaves the number out). Middle band 0.08-0.15 vs flatter and steeper.

claims.claim: More prior touches of the 20 SMA that held = more reliable bounce
claims.test: Rising-20 pullback trades split by how many held touches of the 20 SMA came before in the same trend leg (0, 1, 2, 3+).

claims.claim: Far from the 20 SMA = exit zone, not entry zone
claims.test: Every 3rd bar where the 20 SMA slopes this side's way: forward 12-bar return (in trend direction) by extension decile ((close - 20 SMA) / ATR).
claims.result: 1h top extension decile (median 2.8435 ATR) fwd 0.204% vs middle deciles 0.001% vs bottom decile -0.125%. 15m top -0.016%

claims.claim: Skip the first pullback after the trend accelerates; it fails more than later ones
claims.test: Pullback trades after a 3+ ATR extension in the same leg (threshold: video leaves it out). First pullback vs 2nd and later.

claims.claim: The 200 SMA acts as support / resistance (price bounces off it)
claims.test: Price closes under (over) a line 10 bars, then tags it. Rejected = moves 1.5 ATR away before 1.5 ATR through. Same test on placebo lines = 200 SMA shifted +-3% / +-6%.
claims.result: 1h: 200 SMA rejects 50.3% of tags (n=19754) vs placebo lines 51.6%; magnet 49.3% vs placebo 49.4%; 1d: 200 SMA rejects 47.4% of tags (n=684) vs placebo lines 48.5%; magnet 49.7% vs placebo 51.4%

claims.claim: The 200 SMA is a magnet / natural Target 1
claims.test: From 1-3 ATR away from the line: % of times price reaches the line before moving the same distance the other way (50% = coin flip). 200 SMA vs placebo lines.
claims.result: 1h: 200 SMA rejects 50.3% of tags (n=19754) vs placebo lines 51.6%; magnet 49.3% vs placebo 49.4%; 1d: 200 SMA rejects 47.4% of tags (n=684) vs placebo lines 48.5%; magnet 49.7% vs placebo 51.4%

claims.claim: The 'entry zone' between the 9 EMA and 20 SMA beats entries elsewhere
claims.test: Rising-20 trigger bars (slope > 0.03): low inside the 9/20 zone vs bar that never reached the 9 (shallow) vs bar that broke >0.25 ATR under the 20 (deep). Same entry over bar high, stop bar low, 2R.
claims.result: 1h avg R: zone 0.009 (33.7%), shallow 0.007, deep 0.019; 15m: zone -0.022, shallow -0.025, deep -0.025

left_out_by_video.slope_min: video leaves this out (says 'not flat', ideally '45 degrees'); ATR per bar, 5-bar lookback
left_out_by_video.block200_R: video leaves this out (skip if 200 SMA 'directly above'); 0 = off
left_out_by_video.exit: video leaves this out besides 200 SMA = Target 1; R1.5/R2/R3 fixed or trail under pivots
left_out_by_video.skip_first: accel threshold left out; we use close > 3 ATR past the 20 SMA
left_out_by_video.position size / risk: 1% of equity risked per trade for the curves

takeaways: 'Works on crypto' did not hold up. Every setup was picked on 2020 -> 2024-06 data, then tested on 2024-07 -> 2026-10: base +0.58R -> -0.05R, pullback +0.39R -> +0.01R, pullback_us_session -0.66R -> -0.58R, swing_reclaim20 +1.10R -> -0.13R per trade after costs.
Share of all swept configs that made money out of sample (pooled, after costs): {'base': '11%', 'pullback': '4%', 'pullback_us_session': '0%', 'swing_reclaim20': '12%'}.

The in-sample wins were mostly the 2020-21 crypto bull run plus trailing stops: random entries with the same exits also made money in-sample (base +0.21R), (pullback +0.10R), (swing_reclaim20 +0.37R).

His day-trade version (US session, 1m/2m/5m by time of day, 13:30-20:00 UTC DST aware) is close to break-even before costs (+0.06R OOS) but costs eat it alive (-0.58R): stops under a 1m/2m bar are tiny, so 0.14% round trip is a big chunk of R.
Claims scoreboard: 0 VERIFIED, 7 BUSTED, 1 MIXED out of 8. The MAs barely sort good entries from bad on crypto; the 200 SMA acts like any other line (placebo lines bounce just as often).

Higher time frames hurt less: zero-cost avg R climbs from 5m to 4h, and the HTF-alignment filter and trailing exit are the only knobs that help on average. Still not enough to beat costs out of sample.
Spot cross check (BTC/ETH/SOL, same swing_reclaim20 rules, full history): spot and perp agree in sign, so the result is not a perp quirk.
